# incident_catalog_entry_extension (Resource)

This resource extends a catalog entry that already exists, usually one that incident.io
syncs, such as a schedule, escalation path or user. The sync creates and deletes those
entries, and owns their name, external ID, aliases and synced attributes, so you can't
manage them with `incident_catalog_entry`.

Terraform finds the entry rather than creating it, and writes only:

- `custom_aliases`: aliases your organisation adds to the entry, which syncs keep.
- `attribute_values`: attributes you added to the catalog type yourself, for example in
  the incident.io web UI. Terraform doesn't touch any attribute you don't list.

Terraform never creates or deletes the entry. If no entry matches `identifier`, it fails.
When you destroy the resource, or stop setting something, Terraform clears what it wrote
and leaves the entry in place. Nothing stops people editing the entry in the dashboard:
Terraform puts back what it owns on the next apply.

Changing `custom_aliases` on the User type, or on another type that team membership passes
through, needs an API key with the `team.memberships_update` scope ("Update team
memberships"), because aliases on those entries decide who belongs to a team.

## Example Usage

```terraform
data "incident_catalog_type" "schedule" {
  type_name = "Schedule"
}

data "incident_schedule" "primary_on_call" {
  name = "Primary on-call"
}

# An attribute you added to the Schedule type in the incident.io web UI.
data "incident_catalog_type_attribute" "schedule_runbook" {
  catalog_type_id = data.incident_catalog_type.schedule.id
  name            = "Runbook"
}

# Extend the schedule's catalog entry, which incident.io syncs, with extra aliases
# and a runbook link. Terraform never creates or deletes the entry.
resource "incident_catalog_entry_extension" "primary_on_call" {
  catalog_type_id = data.incident_catalog_type.schedule.id

  # A schedule's catalog entry has the schedule's ID as its external ID.
  identifier = data.incident_schedule.primary_on_call.id

  custom_aliases = ["primary", "pd-primary-on-call"]

  attribute_values = [
    {
      attribute = data.incident_catalog_type_attribute.schedule_runbook.id
      value     = "https://runbooks.example.com/primary-on-call"
    },
  ]
}
```

<!-- schema generated by tfplugindocs -->
## Schema

### Required

- `catalog_type_id` (String) The ID of the catalog type the entry belongs to.
- `identifier` (String) Finds the entry to extend: its ID, external ID or one of its aliases (or its name, if the type uses names as identifiers). For a schedule or escalation path, use its ID. Terraform fails if no entry, or more than one, matches.

### Optional

- `attribute_values` (Attributes Set) Values for attributes you added to the catalog type. Terraform owns only the attributes listed here, and clears an attribute when you remove it. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--attribute_values))
- `custom_aliases` (Set of String) Aliases your organisation adds to the entry. incident.io syncs keep them, and the entry lists them in its aliases too. Only catalog types that incident.io syncs take custom aliases.

When set, Terraform owns the entry's whole custom alias list: it removes custom aliases added elsewhere. Set it to `[]` to clear them. Leave it out of a new resource to leave them as they are.

### Read-Only

- `id` (String) The ID of the catalog entry this resource extends.

<a id="nestedatt--attribute_values"></a>
### Nested Schema for `attribute_values`

Required:

- `attribute` (String) The ID of this attribute, usually loaded from the incident_catalog_type_attribute resource or data source.

Optional:

- `array_value` (List of String) The value of this element of the array, in a format suitable for this attribute type.
- `value` (String) The value of this attribute, in a format suitable for this attribute type.
